Hardware.title: Hardware
Hardware.classification: Current lab reality plus evidence-gated direction
Hardware.summary: Provides the current hardware map without reviving the fixed 2025 Portal/Core/Storage topology as present reality.
Hardware.body:
## Current hardware map

| System | Role | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| **Lenovo Legion Go running Debian** | Active Huey Brain V1 orchestration node | Current lab reality |
| **Huey Body** | Physical robotic shell, formerly Huey Core | Current physical reality; paused for V1 |
| **2017 iMac 5K** | External operator and development tooling | LabTech |
| **Briefcase** | External portable operator/recovery tooling | LabTech |
| **Nexus 5 and Nexus 7 devices** | Replaceable dedicated operator controllers | Maintained targets; validation incomplete |
| **i9 / ASUS TUF / Optane system** | Intended future V4 compute-kernel direction | Requires inventory and integration evidence |
| **Four node-local accelerators** | Candidate future compute posture | Provisional |

## Hardware truth rule

A device is not part of the active Huey node merely because it exists in the lab or appears in an old diagram. Current status requires exact identification, observed condition, assigned role, power and thermal evidence, installation or connection state, test results, and recovery information.

## Safe intake

Record model, revision, serial or inventory identity, photographs, storage, firmware, bootloader, battery, power supply, ports, known damage, starting state, and anything that must be backed up before modification.

Nexus-7-Family.body:
| Variant | Codename | Form factor and role |
|---|---|---|
| 2012 Wi-Fi | `grouper` | Compact tablet status and controller surface |
| 2012 mobile | `tilapia` | Mobile-connected tablet where modem support permits |
| 2013 Wi-Fi | `flo` | Preferred higher-resolution tablet interface |
| 2013 LTE | `deb` | LTE-capable tablet where hardware and carrier conditions permit |

## Tablet advantages

- persistent status, alerts, and history;
- larger diagnostic and service views;
- docked, wall-mounted, or tabletop use;
- richer PyHuey/controller layouts;
- easier review of structured HIMS messages and logs.

## Per-variant rule

Images, kernels, boot paths, cellular support, batteries, cameras, sensors, and repair procedures differ. Each variant needs its own profile and known-limitation record even when the application protocol remains shared.

Tablet layouts must not receive broader authority merely because they display more information.

Hardware-Acceptance-and-Evidence.title: Hardware acceptance and evidence
Hardware-Acceptance-and-Evidence.summary: Provides a reusable staged acceptance model for Body, controller, compute, power, storage, and LabTech hardware.
Hardware-Acceptance-and-Evidence.body:
## Stage 0 — intake and safety

Identify exact model and revision; photograph condition; inspect enclosure, connectors, battery, power supply, cooling, and damage; record firmware, bootloader, storage, and starting state.

## Stage 1 — basic operation and recovery

Establish repeatable boot, shutdown, recovery media, backups, display/input, storage health, networking, charging or power behavior, and thermal observations.

## Stage 2 — assigned role

Install only the software needed for the declared role. Confirm automatic start where required, local diagnostics, version identity, permission boundaries, and failure behavior.

## Stage 3 — integration

Test protocol, authentication, interfaces, error handling, reconnect, logging, and rollback without granting broader authority than the role requires.

## Stage 4 — consequential operation

For physical control, add authorization, interlocks, confirmation, limits, safe-stop, supervised execution, observed result, and retained evidence.

## Stage 5 — repeatability and replacement

Reproduce installation, replace a device, restore from backup or image, revoke old credentials, and confirm that continuity survives hardware loss.

Hardware-Lineage.title: Hardware lineage
Hardware-Lineage.summary: Preserves earlier Portal, Core, Storage Hub, AMD, and custom-kernel work without allowing old diagrams to override present roles.
Hardware-Lineage.body:
The 2025 wiki described a fixed topology built around **Huey-Portal**, **Huey-Core**, **Huey-Legacy**, **Huey-Hub**, and **Storage Hub**, with an AMD-first software stack and a planned October 2025 kernel transition.

That material remains valuable for repair notes, experiments, drivers, topology ideas, and project history. It is not the current architecture by default.

## Current disposition

| Legacy subject | Present treatment |
|---|---|
| iMac 5K Portal instructions | Hardware lineage; the iMac now belongs under LabTech unless a newer explicit role is accepted |
| BD795I-SE/ITX Core topology | Historical experiment; do not present as stable current compute without revalidation |
| AMD GPU tuning | Platform-specific lineage, not project-wide architecture |
| Storage Hub / RAID | Historical infrastructure concept; current backup/storage role must be re-established by evidence |
| custom kernel 6.17 plan | Date-bound 2025 release context |
| hard-coded private network topology | Example lineage, not current configuration |

Preserve exact reports and photographs. Update status instead of deleting history or pretending the old system remains operational.
